name: Côtes de Provence

limits: For red and rosé wine, Cinsault, Grenache, Mourvèdre, Syrah and Tibouren together: at least 70%
For red and rosé wine, Clairette, Sémillon and Ugni Blanc together: at most 10%
For red and rosé wine, Clairette, Sémillon, Ugni Blanc and Vermentino together: at most 20%
For red and rosé wine, Caladoc and Rousseli, each: at most 10%
For white wine, Verdejo, Floreal, Souvignier Gris and Sauvignac together: at most 5%

terms: France's protected place names. A wine sold under one must follow that appellation's rules. The EU's term for the same tier is PDO, or AOP in French.

blurb.text: A Provence appellation with wines made from Cinsault, Grenache, Mourvèdre, Syrah and Tibouren, plus Vermentino, Clairette and Sémillon.

sources.name: Candiago et al. 2022, A geospatial inventory of regulatory information for wine protected designations of origin in Europe, Scientific Data (product specifications as of 2021)
INAO, the appellation's cahier des charges, chapter V (grapes and their shares), from the Bulletin officiel du ministère de l'Agriculture (Licence Ouverte)
Fick and Hijmans 2017, WorldClim 2.1 monthly averages for 1970 to 2000, 2.5 minute grid (about 4.5 km)
Beck et al. 2023, High-resolution (1 km) Koppen-Geiger maps, Scientific Data (1991 to 2020)
Winkler, Cook, Kliewer and Lider 1974, General Viticulture, University of California Press (heat summation regions)
Jones 2010, Climate, grapes, and wine: structure and suitability in a variable and changing climate, VIII International Terroir Congress (which grapes suit which growing season temperatures)
Wikipedia, Appellation d'origine contrôlée (what the label terms mean)
OpenStreetMap contributors, rivers and lakes named on the page (Overpass API), ODbL 1.0
